failing_tests: Update Vendor Scorecard (500 Internal Server Error)

root_cause.description: Database schema defines score as INTEGER, but backend was sending FLOAT values (9.7) causing PostgreSQL to reject the insert

investigation_process.action: Read backend service code for updateVendorScorecard
investigation_process.finding: Previous fix applied numeric parsing (parseFloat) at lines 283-299

investigation_process.action: Read route handler for PUT endpoint
investigation_process.finding: Route handler correctly calls service function with proper parameters

investigation_process.action: Extract test data from Postman collection

investigation_process.finding: Database column is INTEGER, not NUMERIC or FLOAT (line 25)

investigation_process.conclusion: parseFloat(9.7) = 9.7, but PostgreSQL INTEGER column rejects decimal values

solution_implemented.approach: Round decimal scores to integers using Math.round()
rationale: Vendor scorecards use 0-100 rating scale (integers appropriate)
Rounding is user-friendly (accepts both integer and decimal inputs)
No breaking changes to existing integer score submissions

files_modified.change: Split metric_value and score handling, added Math.round() for score only

score_rounding_behavior.note: This was the failing test case

deliverables.purpose: Comprehensive fix documentation with root cause analysis
Structured completion report for Scrum Master

testing.expected_behavior: Score 9.7 will round to 10 and successfully update

next_action: Ready for QA validation - run Postman test suite to confirm 100% pass rate
notes: Root cause was database schema constraint (INTEGER) vs test data (decimal 9.7)
Fix applies to both create and update functions for consistency
metric_value field still accepts decimals (NUMERIC(10,2) in database)
User-friendly: automatically rounds decimal scores without errors

additional_context.why_create_worked: Create test sent score: 10 (integer), which parseFloat converted to 10.0 - PostgreSQL accepted this
